problem: Pre-trained VLN models such as PREVALENT are large and slow, which makes real-time deployment on a robot hard. Earlier non-pretrained VLN methods generalize worse.
motivation: Real-time VLN requires low inference latency and a small model footprint. Pre-training improves generalization, so the paper tries to keep those gains while compressing the model.
key_idea: Compress the PREVALENT pre-trained VLN model with embedding factorization and cross-layer parameter sharing (ALBERT-style) to get a lite real-time model.
insight: Factorized embeddings and parameter sharing remove most of the parameters (77% of the whole model) with almost no loss on Seen Val and about 1-2% loss on Unseen Val, so PREVALENT is heavily over-parameterized. Only the abstract was available, so no ablation detail can be cited.
method: Embedding factorization: decomposes the large embedding matrix into two smaller matrices, cutting embedding parameters by 75%
Parameter sharing: shares parameters across the transformer layers of PREVALENT, cutting total model parameters by 77%
Base model: PREVALENT pre-trained VLN model, with the lite variant trained on the same VLN setup
Efficiency gains: about 17% less training time and 72.2% less inference time

setting.backbone: Lite PREVALENT (factorized embeddings + shared parameters, transformer)
setting.training_data: Presumably PREVALENT-style pre-training and R2R fine-tuning; not stated in the abstract
setting.observation: panoramic RGB with language instruction (presumed, as in PREVALENT)

numbers_note: abstract only; the abstract gives no exact SR/SPL values, only relative statements (consistent on Seen Val, about 1%-2% loss on Unseen Val)
results: The lite model has 75% fewer embedding parameters and 77% fewer total parameters than PREVALENT. It saves about 17% of training time and 72.2% of inference time. SR and SPL match the original on Seen Val, and Unseen Val loses about 1%-2%.
limitations: Only a slight performance drop on Unseen Val (about 1-2%), so the compression is not lossless in generalization
Efficiency is shown only against PREVALENT; there is no on-robot real-time test evident in the abstract
